# Rough-In Redlines

> PDF markup for the trades: electricians, mechanical and plumbing contractors, estimators and project managers. Redline drawings, place trade symbols, count devices, measure to scale and send the office a PDF they can keep editing in Bluebeam or Acrobat. One-time price, no subscription. Made by RK Technology LLC (North Dakota, USA).

## Platforms (as of October 2026)

- Windows 10 and 11: available now on the Microsoft Store (also a standard Windows installer).
- iPad, iPhone and Mac (Apple silicon): coming soon to the App Store. Not available yet.
- Android tablets: in development. Not available yet.

## Pricing

- Free: every tool on up to 3 drawings. No account, no sign-up.
- Rough-In Pro for Windows: $39.99 USD, one-time purchase, unlimited drawings, license key by email that works on 2 PCs. No subscription.
- Crew (team version): coming soon, $15 per person per month. Not available yet.

## Features in the current Windows version

- Clouds, pen, highlighter, text and callouts
- Electrical and trade symbols (600+ in 18 libraries), stamps and signatures
- Photos pinned on the drawing
- Count and Find & Count (box one symbol, find the rest on every sheet); counts export to CSV
- Measure in feet and inches, with the scale read from the title block
- Compare two drawing revisions
- Redact (removes the content underneath)
- Fill PDF forms
- PDF export with markups that stay editable in Bluebeam Revu and Adobe Acrobat
- Panel schedules (iPad; Windows in the next update)
- Pages view, combine files, print and plot (up to 36x48)
- Works offline; files stay on your device; no account needed for Free or Pro

## Coming in the next update (not available yet)

- Snap to the drawing (line ends, corners, crossings)
- Area in square feet
- Lengths shown on lines and boxes while drawing
- Align and group markups
- Symbols snap into evenly spaced rows
- Search text across sheets
- Local projects

## What it is not

- Not CAD: it marks up PDFs and pictures, it doesn't draw or edit DWG files.
- Not a plan room or document-control platform (RFIs, submittals, transmittals).
- Not estimating software with cost databases.
